name: Cao-Zhai (JTNB 1998): squarefree [n^c], optimal error exponent theta*(c) = 36(c+1)/97
comment: Transcription of Cao-Zhai, 'The distribution of square-free numbers of the form [n^c]', J. Theor. Nombres Bordeaux 10 (1998) 287-299. MIN-MAX instance: minimize theta such that every displayed term of Lemma 13 (displays 4.10-4.12, cases i-iii) and Lemma 14 (display 4.13) is <= x^theta. Block variables: theta; zeta1 = log_x Z1 and zeta = log_x Z, the paper's case boundaries, here FREED so the certificate tests whether the paper's choices are optimal. Conventions: Y = x^{c/3} substituted per (4.1) and Lemma 14's N <= x^{c/3} (design choice, pinned); dyadic worst-endpoint substitution per the paper's own displays; epsilon/log powers dropped; exponent pairs (13/31,16/31), (11/53,33/53), (2/7,4/7) enter as fixed rational constants of the cited atoms. Expected: theta*(c) = 36(c+1)/97, reaching 1 exactly at c = 61/36 (the Theorem's threshold). Provenance per group: e1 <- (4.10) case (i) at M = Z1; t1-t5 <- (4.11) case (ii) endpoints; u1-u7 <- (4.12) case (iii); s1-s3 <- (4.13) Sigma_2.
